name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela (Bete Giyorgis)
description: Eleven monolithic medieval Christian churches chiseled out of solid volcanic basalt bedrock, connected by subterranean stone trenches and catacombs.
history: Built by King Lalibela to create a 'New Jerusalem' in Ethiopia after Muslim conquests halted pilgrimage routes to the Holy Land.
construction: Chiseled vertically down into living reddish volcanic tuff; Bete Giyorgis (Church of St. George) was carved as a perfect Greek cross 12 meters deep without adding any external stones or mortar.
architecture: Features intricate Greek and Maltese cross reliefs, arched windows, and subterranean drainage conduits.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978; an eighth wonder of medieval religious engineering.
currentStatus: Active pilgrimage site in Amhara Region, Ethiopia.
